git.link.noGitText: Git is not in your PATH. Install Git for Windows and restart CommandDeck.
git.link.doneText: This folder is already linked to {remote}. The git buttons are in the run section.
git.link.initText: This folder is not under version control. I will only run git init — what goes into your first commit is up to you. Add a .gitignore first if this folder holds node_modules or build output.
git.link.commitText: The repository is empty. Make a commit first, then you can link and push.
git.link.nameText: What should the repository be called?
git.link.visText: {naam} will be created and pushed right away.
git.link.ghMissingText: Without gh I cannot create the repository myself. Create it on github.com — empty, no README — then paste the address.
git.link.urlText: Paste the https url, the ssh form, or just user/repo.
git.link.urlBadText: That does not look like a repository address. Expected something like https://github.com/user/repo.git or user/repo.
git.commit.title: Record your changes
git.commit.text: {aantal} file(s) will be included. What was this change about? Leave it empty and the grey example is used.
git.push.title: Push?
git.push.textEerste: {branch} does not track anything yet. This push sets {remote}/{branch} as upstream, so pull and push work on their own afterwards.
git.stash.title: Set work aside?
git.stash.text: {aantal} file(s) will leave your folder and go into the stash. New files are included. You get them back with the "restore stash" button, which appears on its own.
git.stashLijst.leegTekst: There is currently nothing in this project's stash.
git.stashLijst.kiesTitel: Which one do you want back?
git.stashLijst.kiesTekst: There are {aantal} stashes waiting. The top one is the newest.
git.stashLijst.kiesTekstMeer: There are {aantal} stashes waiting; these are the {getoond} newest. Get the rest back from the terminal.
git.stashLijst.actieTekst: {omschrijving} — {aantal} file(s). Restoring puts them back in your folder and clears the stash.
git.stashLijst.actieTekstBotsing: {omschrijving} — {aantal} file(s). Careful: you are currently working in {botsend} of them. Git refuses to overwrite those, so restoring will probably do nothing. Record your current work first, or set it aside.
git.stashLijst.geweigerdTekst: Git did nothing: these files hold work in your folder that would be overwritten. Nothing changed and {ref} is still there. Record your current changes with commit first, then try again.
git.stashLijst.dropTekst: {omschrijving} is gone for good. This cannot be undone — these changes exist nowhere else.
git.stashLijst.conflictTekst: In {aantal} file(s) your stash touches the same lines as what is in your folder now. Git left markers in them and kept {ref} — so your work is not lost. Resolve it in your editor or in Claude Code; after that you can discard the stash here.
git.block.schoonText: There is nothing to record or set aside.
git.block.geen-commitsText: Nothing to push: this repository has no commits at all.
git.block.niets-vooruitText: You have no commits the remote does not already have.
git.ind.aheadTitle: commits the remote does not have yet
git.ind.behindTitle: commits on the remote you do not have yet (only updated after a fetch)
git.ind.dirtyTitle: changed or new files not recorded anywhere yet
git.ind.noRemoteTitle: this project is not linked to anything yet — use link github
git.ind.noUpstreamTitle: this branch does not track a remote branch yet; the first push sets that up
git.afsluit.titel: {project} has work that exists nowhere else
git.afsluit.tekst: If you close CommandDeck now, this stays on this pc only.
git.afsluit.misluktTekst: There is still work in {project} that exists nowhere else. The push probably failed — check the output.
git.stashMelding.tekst: Windows shut down while there was unrecorded work. It was stashed per project. Those projects now show a "restore stash" button in the row.
git.ident.ontbreektTekst: Git does not know who you are, so it refuses to commit ("Author identity unknown"). Set a name and email address first; they go into the history.
git.ident.ontbreektTekstProfielen: Git does not know who you are, so it refuses to commit. Pick a profile, or set a name once.
git.ident.vraagNaamTitel: Under which name do you commit?
git.ident.vraagNaamTekst: This name goes into the history with every commit. Usually your own name.
git.ident.vraagEmailTekst: GitHub links your commits to your account through this address. Use the address that belongs to your GitHub account.
git.ident.emailFoutTekst: That does not look like an email address. Expected something like you@example.com.
git.ident.bewaarTitel: Save this as a profile too?
git.ident.bewaarTekst: {naam} <{email}> is now set for this folder. Save it as a profile and you can pick it for other projects, and the app will warn you when a different name shows up somewhere.
git.ident.anderTekst: This folder is set to {naam} <{email}> — that is your profile "{profiel}", but this project belongs to "{verwacht}". You can commit anyway, but the name is then fixed in the history.
git.ident.onbekendTekst: This folder is set to {naam} <{email}>. That belongs to no profile. You can commit anyway, but the name is then fixed in the history.
git.ident.chipMisTitle: no user.name or user.email is set; a commit will be refused here
git.ident.chipFoutTitle: you commit here as {naam} <{email}> — that is not the profile this project belongs to
git.profiel.toepassenTitel: Set this profile on this folder?
git.profiel.toepassenTekst: From now on you commit in {map} as {naam} <{email}>. This sets user.name and user.email in .git/config, so it also applies when you commit outside CommandDeck.
git.profiel.ghTekst: Signing in here goes through the GitHub CLI, which decides for itself which account is used. Do you want to switch that to {naam} as well? This opens a terminal, because gh may ask for confirmation.
settings.git.label: On closing
settings.git.desc: Checks on close whether there is work that exists nowhere else. Also sees changes made outside CommandDeck.
git.achter.tekst: The remote has work you do not have yet. Fetch it now?
git.achter.tekstUitEen: You and the remote have diverged. A pull with --ff-only will refuse; you will have to merge or rebase yourself.
git.achter.uitEenLopend: you also have commits the remote does not have
git.achter.vuil: {aantal} changed file(s) — git refuses to overwrite those
settings.git.fetchLabel: On opening, check for new work on the remote
settings.git.fetchDesc: Silently fetches what changed on the remote, at most once every ten minutes per project. Without this the counter stays at 0, even when something is waiting.
settings.git.profielDesc: Under which name you commit, and which GitHub account belongs to it. You pick one per project; the app warns you when a folder holds a different name.
settings.git.profielEmptyHint: No profiles yet. Without profiles the app leaves your identity alone — except when no name is set at all, because then git cannot commit.
settings.git.profielStdTitle: the default for projects that do not pick one themselves
settings.git.profielIncomplete: both a name and an email address are needed
settings.git.profielRemoveText: {naam} disappears from the list. What is set in your repositories does not change.
settings.git.profielRemoveUsed: {naam} disappears from the list. {aantal} project(s) use this profile; they fall back to the default. What is set in your repositories does not change.
settings.git.inlogAsk: ask for a token every time
settings.git.inlogEerlijk: "Ask every time" turns off the credential manager for that folder, so git asks for a token on each push. That is a speed bump, not security: anyone who can sign in as this Windows user can reach the stored tokens of the other profiles. To really separate two people, separate Windows accounts are the answer.
git.ind.otherLocTitle: another location of this project also has work that exists nowhere else
git.branch.tekst: You are on {branch}. {lokaal} local, {remote} only on the remote.
git.branch.geenKeuze: There is nothing to choose from.
git.branch.kiesMeer: {aantal} branches, the first {getoond} are listed below.
git.branch.nieuwTekst: Branches off {branch}, where you are now. You switch to it right away.
git.branch.naamFoutTekst: Git does not accept spaces or any of ~ ^ : ? * [ \. It also cannot start with a dash or a dot.
git.branch.wisselTekst: A branch that only exists on the remote (☁) is created locally and starts tracking it.
git.branch.zelfdeTekst: This is the branch you are on.
git.branch.vuilTekst: {aantal} file(s) changed. If {branch} touches the same files git refuses to switch and nothing happens. Otherwise your changes come along.
git.branch.mergeKies: Which branch do you want to merge into {branch}?
git.branch.mergeBevestig: {bron} will be merged into {doel}. On a conflict the merge stops halfway and I will tell you where.
git.branch.conflictTekst: Git could not work out {aantal} file(s). You have to resolve those yourself, then commit to finish the merge. Abort with git merge --abort.
git.branch.wegHuidig: You cannot delete the branch you are on. Switch to another one first.
git.branch.wegBevestig: {naam} will be deleted locally. If it is already merged you lose nothing; if not, git refuses and I will ask again.
git.branch.wegRemoteBevestig: {naam} will be deleted from the remote. That applies to everyone using this repository, and it cannot be undone.
git.branch.wegNietSamengevoegdTekst: {naam} has commits that exist nowhere else. Deleting means that work is gone.
git.diff.nieuweKop: --- {aantal} new file(s), not shown in the diff above ---
git.commit.nieuwTekst: {aantal} of the {totaal} files are not under version control yet. They are about to be recorded for the first time — check that nothing is in there that should not be.
git.branch.hoofdtakTekst: {naam} is the branch all your work normally comes together in. Deleting it is possible, but hardly ever what you want — did you mean a different branch?
git.branch.remoteHalenTitel: This branch only exists on GitHub
git.branch.remoteHalenTekst: {remote} does not exist here yet. A local branch {naam} will be created at the commit GitHub is on — which may be older than where you are coming from.
git.branch.eigenWerkTitel: This holds work that exists nowhere else
git.branch.eigenWerkVooruit: {naam} is {aantal} commit(s) ahead of GitHub. Delete it and that work is gone.
git.branch.eigenWerkGeenRemote: {naam} exists nowhere but on this pc. Delete it and everything only on it is gone.
git.branch.ookRemoteTekst: It is gone locally, but {naam} is still there. Leave it and it keeps showing up in the list, ready to be pulled back in.
git.terug.tekst: What do you want to undo?
git.terug.tekstGepusht: Note: your last commit is already on GitHub. Undoing makes your history diverge and the next push will be refused.
git.terug.commitTekst: The commit goes away, your changes stay in your folder. You can commit again afterwards.
git.terug.commitTekstGepusht: The commit goes away locally, your changes stay. But it is already on GitHub: you will be behind and the next push will be refused.
git.terug.berichtTekst: Only the text of your last commit changes; the content stays the same.
git.terug.berichtTekstGepusht: Only the text changes. But this commit is already on GitHub, so your history will diverge and the next push will be refused.
git.terug.weggooiKies: In which file? {aantal} files have changed.
git.terug.weggooiBevestig: Everything you changed in {naam} goes back to the last commit. This is the only one you cannot get back — there is no commit and no stash to fall back on.
git.terug.nieuwTekst: {naam} is not under version control yet, so git has no earlier version to go back to. Delete it yourself in the file explorer.
settings.git.pollDesc: How often the indicator in the project header is updated. Pauses while the window is hidden. Off means: only after a git action or when switching location.
accounts.uitleg: An account is also your git identity: the name on your commits and the GitHub account you push with. Switch account and git switches along.
accounts.eerlijk: Note: this separates content, it does not secure anything. Everything lives in your Windows user folder, so anyone on this Windows login can reach every account. If you really need separation, give everyone their own Windows account.
accounts.toevoegenTekst: What is the name of the person who will use this account?
accounts.naamBezet: That name is already taken, or empty.
accounts.verwijderTekst: {naam} disappears from the list. This account's projects stay on disk — I do not throw away anyone's work.
accounts.bestandBlijft: The project list is still there as {bestand} in the CommandDeck folder. Deleting it is up to you.
accounts.laatsteAccount: This is the last account; there has to be at least one.
accounts.kiesTekst: Pick your account. You get your own projects and git settings.
accounts.pinNieuwTekst: Pick a code of at least {min} characters. Four digits is fine, a word or sentence too — no rules about capitals or punctuation.
accounts.pinHerhaal: Once more, to be sure you have it right.
accounts.pinOngeldig: A code is at least 4 characters. Anything else goes.
accounts.pinVerschilt: The two codes are not the same. Try again.
accounts.pinFout: That is not right. You have {over} tries left.
accounts.pinOp: The PIN is not correct. Nothing was switched.
accounts.eigenPinTekst: As soon as there is a second account the PIN starts to matter. {naam} does not have one yet — we set that first, otherwise you put a lock on one door while the other stands open.
accounts.kiesTekstPin: Pick your account and enter your PIN.
git.inlog.uitleg: Your browser opens and shows a code to enter there. No password passes through CommandDeck and your token is never shown. Afterwards you can link the account to this profile.
git.inlog.geenGhTekst: Logging in to GitHub needs gh, which is not on this pc. I can install it through winget — you see exactly what happens in the terminal.
git.inlog.geenProject: There is no project to run this in yet. Add one first.
git.inlog.klaarTekst: These accounts are ready now: {namen}. Set the right one on your git profile and it will switch along when you change account.
accounts.ghWisselMislukt: Could not switch to GitHub account {naam}. Your name is set correctly, but check who you are pushing as.
accounts.gitNaamTekst: What name should your commits carry? This is what others see in the history.
accounts.gitEmailTekst: Which email address goes with it? GitHub links your commits to this.
accounts.gitGhTekst: Your GitHub username, if you have one. That tells git which account to push with when several are on this pc. Leaving it empty is fine.
accounts.gitOnaf: git identity not filled in yet
accounts.gitHaalTekst: I can fetch your name, email and username from GitHub. Then you do not have to type anything.
accounts.gitHaalTekstGeenGh: I can fetch your details from GitHub. You log in through your browser first — no password passes through this app.
accounts.gitOphalenMislukt: Could not fetch your details. Fill them in yourself instead.
accounts.gitGevondenTekst: Commits will say {naam} <{email}>, pushing goes through {gh}. Set it up like this?
git.inlog.geenWingetTekst: Logging in to GitHub needs gh, which is not on this pc. Winget is missing too, so I cannot install it here. Get it from cli.github.com.
git.inlog.installMislukt: The install did not finish or was cancelled. Check the output for what went wrong — on a work pc winget is often blocked.
